correctness.rationale: The exact component-hit probability for two distinct uniformly sampled seeds is derived from counting excluded pairs. Condition on a Bernoulli hub bridge and independent Bin(n,p) retained leaf counts. The cubic moment calculation gives the displayed difference for all integer n>=1. The sign polynomial is increasing in transmission; evaluating its boundary yields uniform dominance at n=1, a unique quadratic crossing at n=2, and strict hub dominance for n>=3. The large-n gap follows by leading terms. An independent percolation/seed-pair enumeration verified the symbolic polynomial for n=1..6 (907792 seeded graph cases), but the infinite assertion is proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary switchover papers identify and analyze the phenomenon for large random/geometric graphs and sufficient general-graph conditions; their statements do not imply an exact fixed-two-seed double-star ordering, its sole n=2 switch, or its macroscopic positive gap for all larger branches. The precise component expectation and sign classification were searched under bistar, double-star, two-hub, percolation and two-seed aliases with no covering finding. Earlier tree-influence literature could still encode the same result.
residual_risks: The exact expression may follow from earlier, insufficiently indexed tree influence-maximization or reliability-polynomial work; specialist independent priority check is still warranted.
The 2015 multi-seed SIR paper was assessed using its abstract rather than complete full text; its regular-random-graph model is not the present fixed double star.
The result treats expected final size only and cannot be generalized to a stochastic ordering or other seed counts without fresh analysis.
No independent external scientific audit has been carried out.

value.rationale: A pair of dense local hub-and-spoke communities linked by a single bridge is a natural stylized epidemiological bottleneck; the question of when dispersed versus targeted seeding yields larger eventual reach is directly motivated by switchover research. A complete infinite-family classification, unique exact six-vertex switch, and nonzero limiting population-normalized difference identify how a bridge bottleneck can suppress reversal even at arbitrarily high internal degree. It gives a sharp structural counterpoint rather than merely a computed example.
